reading.title: Football Injury
reading.passage: Yesterday Bek played football with his classmates. In the second half, he jumped for the ball and fell. 'Ow! My knee hurts!' he cried. His friend helped him up. At home, Bek put ice on his knee. His mother said: 'Rest today, and your leg will feel better tomorrow.' Bek washed his hands, ate dinner and rested. By morning, the knee felt much better.
qs: What happened to Bek in the second half?
What did he cry?
How did Bek's mother help him?
How did he feel by morning?

ex: I **have a cold** and a **sore throat**.
Bu dorini iching va dam oling.

reading.title: Lola's Sick Day
reading.passage: Lola woke up with a sore throat and a high temperature. 'I have a headache too,' she told her mother. Mother checked her temperature: 38.5 degrees. 'You have a fever. You should stay in bed today,' she said. Lola drank warm tea, took her medicine and slept. By evening, she felt a little better. 'Rest is the best medicine,' her mother smiled.
qs: What did Lola wake up with?
What was her temperature?
What did the mother say?
How did Lola feel by evening?

listening.title: The Phone Call to the Doctor
qs: What is wrong with the boy?
What does the doctor advise?
When should he call again?
listening.script: Listen. Boy: 'My stomach hurts and I feel tired.' Doctor: 'Did you eat something bad?' Boy: 'Maybe.' Doctor: 'Drink warm water and rest. Don't eat heavy food today. If it gets worse, call me tomorrow.'

Doctor: **Take one tablet** twice a day.

reading.title: A Visit to the Doctor
reading.passage: Jasur felt sick, so his mother made an appointment. At the clinic, the receptionist took his card and told him to wait. Soon the doctor called him in. 'What's the problem?' the doctor asked. 'I have a sore throat and a headache,' said Jasur. The doctor examined him and checked his temperature. 'It's just a cold. Take this prescription to the pharmacy. Rest for two days and drink warm tea. You'll recover quickly.' Jasur felt better already.
qs: Who made the appointment for Jasur?
What did the receptionist do?
What did the doctor examine?
What did the doctor tell Jasur to do?

listening.title: At the Pharmacy
qs: How often should the man take the tablets?
How many tablets should he take?
What else should he do?
listening.script: Listen. Pharmacist: 'Here is your medicine. Take one tablet three times a day, after food.' Man: 'Anything else?' Pharmacist: 'Drink plenty of warm water and rest. Keep warm.' Man: 'Thank you!' Pharmacist: 'Get well soon!'

Set up a classroom clinic.

reading.title: The Quick Decision
reading.passage: On Saturday, Umida saw smoke coming from her neighbour's kitchen window. She called 101 immediately and told the operator the address. 'You mustn't go inside,' the operator warned. Umida stayed outside and guided her neighbours to a safe place. When the firefighters arrived, the fire was still small because of her quick call. 'You were brave and calm,' the chief said. Umida smiled. She knew the rules.
qs: What did Umida see?
What number did she call?
What did the operator warn?
Why did the fire stay small?

listening.title: The Emergency Call

What must the caller do until help arrives?
listening.script: Listen. Operator: 'Emergency, which service?' Caller: 'There's a car accident on Mustaqillik street!' Operator: 'Is anyone hurt?' Caller: 'Yes, a man is hurt.' Operator: 'Stay calm. Don't move him. An ambulance is coming now.'

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner

teacher: Teach real emergency numbers and when to call.

Role-play the emergency call — students remember this.

lessons.title: Career Dreams
goals: 💭 Express dreams: 'I want to be a...'
warmup: 🌟 Dream jobs
What do you want to be? / Nima bo'lmoqchisiz?
💭 Jobs review
Name 5 jobs from L46. / L46 kasblarini ayting.

x: I want a career in medicine.
My dream is to be a pilot.
I want to become a doctor.
The scientist works in a lab.
Doctors are very useful for society.

grammar.rule: Dreams: **I want to be a... / I'm going to be a... / I'd like to...** + reason with because
ex: I **want to be** a programmer **because** I love computers.
Dasturchi bo'lmoqchiman, chunki kompyuterlarni yaxshi ko'raman.
She **is going to be** a doctor.
mistake: Right: *I want to become a doctor.*

reading.title: Three Dreams
reading.passage: Three friends, three dreams. Dilnoza wants to be a doctor because she likes helping sick people. She studies biology every day. Bobur is going to be a programmer — he loves computers and games, and wants to create his own game one day. Aziz dreams of being a pilot. He watches planes at the airport and reads about flying. Their teacher says: 'Dreams are important. Work hard, and they will come true.'
qs: Why does Dilnoza want to be a doctor?
What does Bobur want to create?
What does Aziz dream of?
What does the teacher say?

lessons.title: At Work
goals: 🕘 Talk about working hours and duties
Ish vaqti va vazifalar haqida gapirish
warmup: 💼 Working people
What jobs have we learned? / Qaysi kasblarni bildik?
🕘 Work hours
When does your father start work? / Otangiz ishni soat nechada boshlaydi?

x: I have to wake up at 6.
She doesn't have to work on Sunday.
My duty is to answer calls.
We have a meeting every Monday.
My boss is strict but fair.

grammar.rule: **have to + verb** (necessary) · **don't/doesn't have to + verb** (not necessary)
grammar.uz: 'have to' — majburiyat; 'don't have to' — shart emas
ex: She **doesn't have to** work on Friday.
We **have to** finish the report today.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I ___ wake up at 6. (have to/has to)
She ___ wear a uniform. (has to/have to)
We ___ work overtime. (don't have to/has to)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Not necessary means: → a) don't have to b) have to c) must

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: wear / to / a / I / uniform / have / .
has / She / to / calls / answer / .

reading.title: A Nurse's Day
reading.passage: Malika is a nurse at a city hospital. She has to wake up at five o'clock and be at work by seven. She has to wear a clean uniform and check the patients in her ward. Some days she works overtime when there are many patients. She doesn't have to work on Saturdays — that is her rest day. Malika loves her job. 'I have to be kind and careful every day,' she says. 'My colleagues help me, and my boss is fair.'
qs: What time does Malika have to wake up?
What does she have to wear?
When doesn't she have to work?
What does Malika love about her job?

listening.title: The New Job
qs: What time does the man have to start?

When doesn't he have to work?
listening.script: Listen. 'So, you are the new employee. You have to start at 8 o'clock and wear a uniform. You don't have to work on Sundays. On Fridays we have a short meeting.' 'Do I have to work overtime?' 'Only in busy weeks.' 'OK, I understand. Thank you!'

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 work words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences with have to · Reading: re-read 'A Nurse's Day' · Speaking: describe your parent's job.
teacher: Contrast must (strong) vs have to (daily need).
